text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High error rate and sustained latency on /v1/generate for model=qwen-43m-mqa (kv cache pressure). Auto-alert triggered: 5xx spike + token-outage.

alex: I'm on it. paging rotation: alex (oncall). any immediate customer reports?

maria: seeing a sudden growth in KV cache size on the inference-workers for qwen-43m-mqa, plus continuous-batching backlog. Heap + GPU memory climbing then OOMs.

chen: hm, qwen MQA has known dense KV per-request patterns, GQA mismatch can blow up prefix caching if MQA/GQA flags mix. Are we rolling a mixed model variant in the same pool?

alex: checking pool routing now. seems qwen-43m-mqa and qwen-43m-gqa were both routed to the same dedicated pool by the recent rollout 1748459000.

sam: @alex customer-impact: two startups have 5xx alerts (prod traffic) and one support ticket. latency spikes ~1-2m windows. customers affected: prod-only deployments hitting streaming endpoints.

irene: CS pinged the three affected customers, letting them know we're investigating. No data loss reported but elevated latencies.

maria: metrics snapshot: kv_cache_entries per worker jumped 8x in 30s; continuous_batcher queue length up 400%. Workers dropping to 70% GPU mem free then OOM. Rolling restarts would not help until we stop the bad traffic pattern.

alex: immediate mitigation idea: 1) disable prefix/KV caching for qwen-43m-mqa in that pool 2) tighten continuous_batcher max_batch_tokens to 128 3) drain mixed-pool routing to fallback pool with dedicated qwen-gqa variant. Anyone object?

chen: +1 disable cache for mqa variant. Also set batch max tokens and disable cross-model pooling — MQA's KV growth is per conversation when combined with GQA because key-embedding format incompatible and we keep duplicating cache entries.

sam: do we have a fast toggle in Console or do we need config push? I can approve a temp config change from product.

alex: we have runtime flags per-route. I can flip in <2m. Will apply to the affected route in region us-west-2 first.

deploy-bot: Starting config change: PATCH /config/routes/qwen-43m-mqa - {"kv_cache.enabled": false, "continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens": 128} by alex at 1748501352

deploy-bot: Config change applied to pool redwood-dedicated-usw2-3. Rolling update to 6 workers.

maria: seeing immediate drop in kv_cache_entries growth on those workers. queue length for batcher down ~60% within 45s. Error rate dropping.

alex: switching routing: moving qwen-43m-gqa to separate pool to avoid mixed-variant co-location. Command: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/route/migrate \\  -d '{"model":"qwen-43m-gqa","target_pool":"redwood-dedicated-usw2-gqa"}' \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN"
```

deploy-bot: Migration job queued id=job_98321, estimated 45s

maria: watch logs: inference-worker-07 still shows some eviction churn but overall mem pressure trending down. 5xx at 0.8% now (was 9%).

chen: note for postmortem: MQA uses variable-sized KV proto vs GQA fixed layout; when both variants served in same pool our caching key computation dedup logic failed and we kept separate entries for identical prefixes -> cache blowup. We've seen this pattern in staging but didn't simulate traffic mix.

sam: customer impact update: two customers saw transient 5xx (12-30s per request window). retry logic kicked in, most requests succeeded on retry. One support ticket escalated to SE.

irene: CS sent mitigation email and temporary ETA: 30m. customers asked for root cause; I'll wait for confirmed fix before final note.

alex: monitoring: p95 latency back to baseline; function-calls success rate 99.2%. I'll leave the cache disabled for qwen-mqa and keep batch_tokens at 128 for next 2 hours, then we can assess metrics.

maria: recommended hotfix for next deploy: add model-variant tag check to caching key generator and enforce cross-variant isolation in pool assignment. For immediate safety, add a runtime guard: if pool has >1 variant with incompatible-kv then disable prefix cache automatically.

chen: agree. I'll open a follow-up PR to change key derivation and add tests with mixed-variant load generator. tagging this as blockers/kv-caching.

sam: good. for customer comms I'll draft a short update after we confirm stable for 30m.

alex: handing off to night oncall @maria in 20m. maria, I left runbook steps in #oncall-runbooks and the timeline of changes in the incident doc.

maria: ack. I'll keep watch for 1 hour, then escalate to eng-oncall if we see reversion. Adding follow-up tasks: 1) patch caching key derivation (chen) 2) auto-guard at config layer (maria) 3) create e2e mixed-variant test (qa) 4) postmortem scheduled.

deploy-bot: Migration job job_98321 succeeded at 1748501705. Pools separated.

maria: final check: 5xx baseline <0.5%, batch queue normal, kv_cache entries stable. Marking incident as mitigated but not resolved until code fix merged.

alex: thanks team. opening incident ticket INC-2026-042 and assigning to chen for root cause and to sam for customer notes.

irene: will update customers with mitigation + ETA for permanent fix. they appreciated the quick response. :thumbsup:

chen: starting root cause PR now, will link in the ticket.

alex: closing channel to incidents for now — will reopen if regressions.

(END THREAD)
